chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who takes on a debt and does not have the intention of paying it, he would be at the status of the thief.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: at the status of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a debtor who intends not to repay their loan?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* distinguishes between simple default and fraudulent appropriation by linking the debtor's internal intention (*niyyah*) to the legal category of theft (*sariqah*). This ruling underscores the ethical weight of sincerity in financial contracts, implying that the debt is not merely a civil obligation but a trust (*amanah*) whose breach constitutes a moral transgression akin to stealing property outright.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who takes on a debt and does not have the intention of paying it, he would be at the status of the thief’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from ibn Faddal from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who borrows without the intention to pay back is considered a thief.’”
